subject: Newbie Question -- How to choose Reference for CNAG Non-paired Test,  Affy 500K chip

messages.author: 586f76fbf30bf5f0
messages.subject: Newbie Question -- How to choose Reference for CNAG Non-paired Test,  Affy 500K chip
parts:
Hi All,

I'm a newbie of this forum; also I'm very new to microarray analysis.
I would like to do some learning on using CNV on Autism data. I have
allocated (a) a dataset on GEO that used Affy 500K SNPs chip for
genotyping of trios (probands and some parents). (b) CNAG 2.0. I
would like to apply CNAG2.0 on the data downloaded from GEO, using non-
paired TEST and REFERENCE.

Would the experts tell me:
a. What is Reference used in CNAG?
a.1. Should Reference be genotyped of non-autism (in this case)
individuals, and TEST is for genotyped data of affected (autism)
individuals? Or vice versa? Or it depends on what I would like to
study?
a.2. Does the Reference data need to be 500K as well? can it be
10K? I assume that 500K reference shoudld be preferable.
a.3 Does anyone know where to get 500K Genotyped control data?

b. How does aroma.affymetrix compare to dnaCopy in bioconductor?

Many thanks in advance for any help.

Yoshi C.

On Thu, Feb 28, 2008 at 5:32 PM, Yoshi <Yoshi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi All,
>
> I'm a newbie of this forum; also I'm very new to microarray analysis.
> I would like to do some learning on using CNV on Autism data. I have
> allocated (a) a dataset on GEO that used Affy 500K SNPs chip for
> genotyping of trios (probands and some parents). (b) CNAG 2.0. I
> would like to apply CNAG2.0 on the data downloaded from GEO, using non-
> paired TEST and REFERENCE.

So, first of all, aroma.affymetrix does not do implement the CNAG
model/method explicitly although you could "imitate" it with some
knowledge.

>
> Would the experts tell me:
> a. What is Reference used in CNAG?

CNAG v2 is using the *selected subset* of the *pool of all test
samples* to calculate its reference. Please see the Nannya et al.
(2005) for details.

> a.1. Should Reference be genotyped of non-autism (in this case)
> individuals, and TEST is for genotyped data of affected (autism)
> individuals? Or vice versa? Or it depends on what I would like to
> study?

I'm not sure what you are asking here and especially what you mean by
"vice versa".

To do copy number analysis you do *not* have to genotype your arrays.
It has been suggested that this can improve the power, but most models
do not require genotype calls, including CNAT, CNAG, dChip, and CRMA
(Bengtsson et al 2008; see website).

> a.2. Does the Reference data need to be 500K as well? can it be
> 10K? I assume that 500K reference shoudld be preferable.

Yes. Since the raw CNs are calculated as a ratio between test and
reference at every locus, you need a reference estimate at each locus
of your test sample. For many different reasons, I do not see that it
is possible to extrapolate from a lower-density array, actually not
even from a higher-density array.
> a.3 Does anyone know where to get 500K Genotyped control data?

>
> b. How does aroma.affymetrix compare to dnaCopy in bioconductor?

aroma.affymetrix is an R framework to do various modeling of
Affymetrix data, e.g. several different normalization methods are
available as well as probe-summarization models. For CN analysis,
aroma.affymetrix implements, via wrappers to existing, the GLAD
('GLAD' package) and CBS ('DNAcopy' package) segmentation methods.
So, given the same raw CN estimates, aroma.affymetrix gives identical
CN regions as if you would have called CBS of DNAcopy explicitly.

What we this far have achieved and what is implemented in
aroma.affymetrix is an preprocessing method called CRMA (Bengtsson et
al 2008) that provides improved raw CN estimates that hopefully allows
the segmentation methods downstream to perform better.

Hope this helps

/Henrik
